seen.extent: 1 leaf, 2 images. Image 1: about 37 lines, clear Castilian with cipher runs on most lines, dated Dueñas 7 Oct 1470. seen.cipher: Signs, digits and letter-like characters set inside clear Castilian (syllabic or nomenclator type, probably with nulls). A second, smaller and quicker hand has written glosses between the lines over many cipher runs and in the margins where the interline is short (legible example: onze leguas); some glosses are struck through and rewritten. At the zoom used here, several long cipher runs between glosses carry no gloss, so the decipherment on the leaf is partial; I could not establish that every group is glossed. A decipherment is therefore written on the leaf.

prior_art.tomokiyo: cryptiana.web.fc2.com index (crypto.htm, read 4 Nov 2026) has Italian cipher pages (Papal ciphers during the Western Schism, Ciphers of Isabella d Este, Venetian ciphers and others) and no Medici or Michelozzi page.
prior_art.lasry: No Lasry or HistoCrypt reading of Lorenzo de Medici letters found in the 4 Nov 2026 searches (results: Simonetta on Montefeltro 1478, Vito).
prior_art.edition: Lorenzo de Medici, Lettere: the Warwick Italian Elites index cites Lettere VIII (Butters, Giunti 2001, 1484-85) for Michelozzi at the camp in 1484, and a library catalogue lists vol. VII as 1482-1484; the 28 Jul 1484 letter falls in VII or VIII. Vol. VII is on the Internet Archive only as a lending-library item (bwb_KU-999-231, access restricted, login needed), vol. VIII is print only; neither was opened. Lettere VI printed its cipher slip deciphered (lead 1552), so the edition probably prints this one.
prior_art.literature: Marco Vito (Vienna) project on the encrypted Medici documents of 1486-1491 and his 2025 papers (NEALT Proceedings, Tartu, A Florentine polyalphabetic cipher in the 15th century; Nuova Rivista Storica Militare) found by search; none treats this letter as far as the search shows, overlap not excluded.

vetting.key_check: No key tried. The Ginori Conti 29.114.a key sheets (Otto di Pratica, Dieci di Balia) named by the lead and any ASF Florentine chancery keys on DECODE were not tested; the glosses on the leaf would be the first source for rebuilding the key.

seen.where: BNCF TECA image viewer https://teca.bncf.firenze.sbn.it/ImageViewer/servlet/ImageViewer?idr=BNCF0003827859 (Ginori Conti 29.136), opened in Chrome on 4 Nov 2026 without login; the spread with c. 1v (address Nicolao Michelozzo, Johanni Antonio Aretino, Roma) and c. 2r viewed and zoomed (cc. 2v-3v not opened).
seen.extent: c. 2r: a dense page of 40 or more lines, clear Italian with cipher groups of digits and signs on most lines; the 8 Jan biglietto on cc. 1r-v is separate. The date 5 Feb 1490 is the catalogue date; I did not read it on the leaf.
seen.cipher: Cipher groups of digits and signs inside the Italian text; a smaller hand has written interlinear glosses above and below many groups (zoomed: short words such as ogni S. S. and mentione); not every group carries a gloss as far as seen. So a partial decipherment is written on the leaf.
